name: Elliptic Curve Cryptography Assessment
description: Assessment of elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) implementations including ECDSA, ECDH, EdDSA (Ed25519, Ed448), and curve selection. Covers curve parameter validation, nonce generation for ECDSA, invalid curve attacks, twist security, and implementation quality review.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to elliptic curve cryptography assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands ECC fundamentals and why curve selection matters
evidence: Can explain elliptic curve operations at a conceptual level
Understands the security advantage of ECC over RSA at equivalent key sizes
Can name common curves (P-256, P-384, Curve25519) and their use cases

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies ECC configurations and curve selections under supervision
evidence: Extracts ECC parameters from certificates and key exchange negotiations
Identifies use of weak or non-standard curves under guidance
Documents ECC configuration findings following lab templates
Uses OpenSSL and similar tools to inspect ECC key parameters

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses ECC implementations for correctness and known vulnerabilities
evidence: Evaluates ECDSA implementations for nonce quality (k-value reuse, biased nonces)
Identifies invalid curve attack vectors in ECDH implementations
Assesses curve selection against current standards (NIST, SafeCurves criteria)
Produces findings with clear remediation paths referencing FIPS 186-5, SP 800-186 (curve parameters), or equivalent

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex ECC assessment scenarios; demonstrates advanced attacks in lab
evidence: Demonstrates ECDSA nonce-reuse key recovery in lab environment
Evaluates ECC implementations for timing and power analysis side-channels
Assesses EdDSA (Ed25519/Ed448) implementations for cofactor handling and malleability
Reviews and mentors junior staff on ECC assessment techniques

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines ECC assessment methodology; recognised authority on ECC security
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's ECC assessment methodology
Published research on ECC implementation vulnerabilities or novel attacks
Provides expert consultation on curve selection and ECC migration strategies
Trains teams on ECC internals, mathematical foundations, and assessment approaches

assessment_methods.description: Assess an ECDSA implementation: evaluate curve selection, nonce generation, and signature verification; demonstrate nonce-reuse key recovery on a lab target
Given a custom ECDH implementation, identify whether it is vulnerable to invalid curve attacks and propose mitigations
